messages:
maya: FYI I opened a draft PR to simplify the quickstart into a one-file 'pilot' hello app that covers local tokenless dev, env var fallback, and a tiny Docker deploy for Dedicated customers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3587
liam: nice. Do we deprecate the old multi-file tutorial or keep it linked?
tara: let's keep a link to the full app repo for folks who want the deeper layout. for the main quickstart, single-file is easier to scan.
jordan: can we include a compact SDK init example showing env fallback + async usage? something like:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || undefined });
const res = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rwd-3b', input: 'Hello world' });
console.log(res.output[0].text);
```
maya: that's in the draft. I also added a short note about KMS-backed secrets for Dedicated and a one-liner healthcheck for containerized runs.
liam: CI flagged code-fence language consistency (js vs javascript). Updated the PR to standardize on "js".
maya: thanks, fixed linting in the last commit and pushed. pinging @docs-review for copy & accessibility pass.
docs-bot: CI: docs build started ⚙️ — preview will be posted when ready.
sarah: small suggestion: under "auth setup" add a tiny troubleshooting table: common env mistakes and quick verification commands. I'll draft it and push.
tara: sweet. Also, in the runtime section please call out default sequence length and when to pick quantized model builds for local checks.
jordan: adding a short note about quantization tradeoffs (speed vs fidelity) and when to use rwd-3b-quant for quick local smoke tests.
maya: assigning follow-ups: @sarah adds troubleshooting table, @jordan adds quantization note, @liam verifies links to SDK changelog and examples. After those commits I'll request final review.
liam: I'll run linkcheck and scan for outdated example URLs tonight.
sarah: pushed troubleshooting table and a link to the healthcheck example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/hello-healthcheck. Also added a tiny FAQ bullet about expired tokens.
maya: PR updated, running a quick local build. If Netlify preview looks good we can merge and backport to 2.1-stable. tagging rc.
pr-bot: PR #3587 requested reviewers: liam, jordan, sarah
liam: approved in GH. :thumbsup:
jordan: reviewed and pushed a couple micro-edits to the runtime blurb.
sarah: small copy tweak to the troubleshooting table committed.
ci-bot: Preview build succeeded ✅ — netlify preview: https://deploy-preview-3587--docs.redwood.ai
maya: merging once the canary smoke pass finishes. Great work everyone :rocket:
ci-bot: canary smoke checks passed. Merge complete. Backporting to branch 2.1-stable scheduled.
